scope.decision: Review only the generic Node detached-child contrast within the external private Windows Job.
excluded: Native DSH SDK semantics or capability; not reviewed here
Other runtimes, spawn methods, Windows versions, or arbitrary hostile code
Changes to frozen job-review.json or Job source files

recommendation.rationale: On the tested Windows host, the Node driver exits successfully while its detached synthetic leaf remains alive and is the sole member reported by the external private Job; closing that Job makes the retained leaf HANDLE signaled.
caveats: This is a Node v24.16/libuv plus synthetic child observation, not proof about native DSH SDK or every detached-child pathway.
The Node/libuv global Job and this Python-owned external Job are distinct layers; the fixture demonstrates the external Job cleanup boundary only.
The result is bounded to the tested host and the current exact source pins.

sourceReview.finding: Builds a synthetic Node fixture that spawns a detached child, unrefs it, and lets the driver naturally exit.

Runs fixture through the trusted gate inside the external owned Job; waits for driver exit; checks the external Job has exactly the leaf PID; observes leaf alive; closes Job and waits on retained process HANDLE for signaled result.
Finally path closes the owned Job again idempotently, stores raw stdout/stderr and summary, and reports run result.

interpretation: Node v24.16 libuv assigns non-detached uv_spawn children to its own global Job but skips that assignment for UV_PROCESS_DETACHED. In the cited detached branch it sets DETACHED_PROCESS and CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP, not CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB. The fixture independently demonstrates that this detached Node leaf remains in the separate external Job on this host and is killed when that external Job is closed.

officialReferences.supports: Detached flag uses DETACHED_PROCESS and CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP; source says it does not set CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB.
Only non-detached uv_spawn children are explicitly assigned to libuv global Job; assignment failure behavior is documented in source.
Windows Job Objects manage process groups, default child association, and kill-on-close behavior.
